prediction:
#10's Y16 class. THE BRIEFED PREMISE IS WRONG AND THAT COMES FIRST. I was told "a HILO mapping over Y16 has one 16-bit field where the mapping wants two". No capture stands behind that. Test16bit -- the only STAGE_DOT_PRODUCT/DOT_ST path in Bump map, the one that pushes DOT_RGBMAPPING 0x044 -- is instantiated ONLY for SZ_R16B16 (bump_map_tests.cpp:56-61). Every Y16 and YUV capture goes through the generic Test(), i.e. BUMPENVMAP; and state->tex_hilo16 is set only for SZ_R16B16 and LU_IMAGE_R16B16, so Y16 could not reach dotmap_hilo_1_16 even if it reached a dot stage. Nothing in dotmap_* can address these captures, and dotmap_hilo_1's deliberate 8-bit reconstruction is untouched as briefed.

THE MECHANISM. append_bump_channel reads the luminance from view component 0. For SZ_A8/LU_IMAGE_A8 the swizzle is {ONE,ONE,ONE,R} and for SZ_Y16/LU_IMAGE_Y16 it is {ONE,R,R,ONE}; vk/constants.h and gl/constants.h agree, and those four rows are the whole set in either table with a literal in component 0. So component 0 carries no stored data, and RSIGNED has nothing to sign. We signed it anyway, turning bump_unsigned(1.0) = 1.0 into sign3_to_0_to_1(bump_snorm(1.0)) = 0.496. BumpEnvLum ties rsigned to bsigned (bump_env_lum_tests.cpp:163), so exactly the two quads carrying BSIGNED came out low.

MEASURED, not argued, at 0026f00534, quads in (gsigned,bsigned) order, printed by docs/testing/bump_sign_quads.py which is committed with the fix:

  BumpEnvLum_A8   per quad  310 / 14,241 /   422 / 14,187   one step  0 / 13,819 /   0 / 13,765
  BumpEnvLum_Y16  per quad  310 / 13,755 /   422 / 13,645   one step  0 / 13,333 /   0 / 13,223

Every one of those one-step deltas is NEGATIVE -- ours low -- which is the direction a halved luminance predicts and the opposite of what a rounding error would give in both directions. Remove them and each flagged quad is left with exactly 422, the value the unflagged quads of the same capture already hold.

THREE CONTROLS, ALL INSIDE THE CORPUS, NO FLOOR TRANSFERRED FROM ANOTHER CAPTURE. (1) Quad 2 carries GSIGNED on a real data channel and sits at 422 with ZERO one-step px, so a sign flag on stored data is already handled and the defect is not "sign flags on 16-bit formats". (2) Quads 0 and 2 already take the branch this change routes the others to, and they sit at 310 and 422 -- which is what makes 1.0 the MEASURED luminance rather than an assumption I am fitting. (3) BumpMap_A8 is 1,576 with per-quad 310/422/422/422 under the same swizzle and the same flags, differing from BumpEnvLum_A8 only in having no luminance stage at all. That localises the defect to this one channel by a capture rather than by an argument, and it is why components 1 and 2 are deliberately NOT included: BumpMap_A8 takes them from the same literal, under flags, and is already at the floor.

AND THE INSTRUMENT HAS A CONTROL TOO. Hardware's own four quads differ by 0/586/312/612 on every A8, Y16 and R16B16 capture in both suites -- its positional floor -- while on byte texels they differ by 0/586/8,212/8,431 (BumpMap_G8B8) and 0/13,796/312/13,814 (BumpEnvLum_R8B8). So the quad-identity measurement can see a live flag when there is one, and reports these as inert. That is the already-established R16B16 result -- sign extension being a no-op mod 2^16 -- reaching the bump path instead of only the dot path.

LEG L1, THE MECHANISM LEG, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY BASELINE-INDEPENDENT. The captures I derived these numbers from are at 0026f00534, nineteen hw/ commits behind arm A, so absolutes must not be registered (AGENTS.md: register deltas, not absolutes, when the baseline came from a different binary). The leg is therefore a WITHIN-FRAME IDENTITY on arm B, which no baseline can shift: for each of BumpEnvLum_A8, _A8_L, _Y16 and _Y16_L, the two BSIGNED quads ("Gu Bs" and "Gs Bs") have the SAME differing count as the GSIGNED-only quad ("Gs Bu") of the same capture, and ZERO one-step pixels in all four quads. Run docs/testing/bump_sign_quads.py on both arms to check it. At arm A that identity reads 14,241 / 14,187 against 422; at arm B it must read 422 / 422 against 422. THE WORLD IN WHICH IT FAILS: if hardware's luminance for a literal component is some constant other than 1.0, all four quads agree but none of them lands on the unflagged quad's value, so the identity holds and the ABSOLUTE moves -- which is why the second half of the leg is that the one-step count reaches zero rather than merely equalising. And if the one-step class is not the luminance at all, the flagged quads keep a one-step remainder and the identity fails outright.

LEG L2, INTERMEDIATE VALUE, THE HALF THAT CAN FAIL. BumpEnvLum_Y8, _Y8_L, _AY8, _AY8_L and _A8Y8 must NOT move, and must keep their one-step pixels in ALL FOUR quads: measured 7,139 / 7,441 / 7,301 / 7,501 per quad with 6,829 / 7,019 / 6,879 / 7,079 one-step, i.e. spread evenly and not concentrated in the flagged pair. Component 0 for SZ_Y8 is {R,R,R,ONE} and for SZ_AY8 {R,R,R,R} -- real stored data -- so RSIGNED is meaningful there and this gate must not reach them. A fix fitted to "Y-ish formats" rather than to "component 0 is a literal" would drag them along, and their total 29,382 sits only 222 px from A8's 29,160, which is exactly the kind of coincidence of size that invites the wrong rule. Likewise BumpEnvLum_R16B16 is ~20,800 wrong in all four quads and stays there: component 0 for SZ_R16B16 is the G swizzle, real data.

LEG L3, FLAGGED AS TAUTOLOGICAL, DO NOT COUNT IT. "The four captures get better." Any change that stops signing the literal forces that. It is worth asserting that the fix does what I think and it is not a falsifier; L1's within-frame identity is.

LEG L4, THE CONTROL THAT SAYS ONLY THE LUMINANCE MOVED. Every Bump_map capture must be byte-identical, including BumpMap_A8, BumpMap_A8_L, BumpMap_Y16 and BumpMap_Y16_L, because Bump_map uses STAGE_BUMPENVMAP with no luminance and append_bump_channel is never called with comp 0 there. If any of them moves, the claim that this touches one channel is wrong.

LEG L5, THE BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. 1,024 shaders were emitted through both builds over four bump stage modes x all 16 TEXFILTER sign masks x the new gate x snorm_tex x tex_hilo16 x GL and Vulkan, from CLEAN builds of docs/testing/psh_differ both times. 928 are byte-identical, ZERO change with the gate off -- so the gate is measured and not asserted -- and the 96 that change differ by exactly one line, the bumpL assignment, whose three old forms are all replaced by bump_unsigned(t0.r). Texture_format and Texture_signed_component_tests are on the disc for this: the first holds TexFmt_A8/_A8_L/_Y16/_Y16_L at 0 differing px, which are the PINNED swizzle rows this reading depends on, and the second is the other consumer of the TEXFILTER sign bits.

A NOTE ON THE MEASUREMENT ITSELF, because it nearly cost a false report. The first blast-radius sweep was run from an INCREMENTAL psh_differ build, and psh_differ's make regenerates its carved psh.c by mtime, so a source restored with git stash pop can be older than build/psh.o and silently relink the previous object. That produced an apparent 52 probes moving from `changed` to `same`, including fog_mode INVERTING 0-changed/7-same to 7-changed/0-same, which no bump-channel edit can do. The impossible row was the finding; a clean rebuild gave the identical report on both versions, and both sweeps here were then re-run from clean and reproduced to the shader. Recorded in docs/testing/psh_differ/README.md.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT CONCLUDE. The four YUV captures (BumpMap_UYVY_L, _YUY2_L, BumpEnvLum_UYVY_L, _YUY2_L) are 111,496 px each with max|d| 127 and ZERO one-step, wrong in all four quads at ~27,900 each, and their masks are byte-identical across both suites and both byte layouts -- a mask invariant to the stage and to the source data is geometry, so it is the whole drawn area. TexFmt_UYVY_L and TexFmt_YUY2_L are 0 differing px, so the decode is bit-exact and this is not a decode defect. I did not determine the mechanism and I am not guessing at it. The cheapest next measurement, which needs no device: the YUV formats pack two pixels per four bytes with U and V shared across a horizontal pair, so stage 0's texel under that subsampling is the one thing here that behaves differently from every other format; compute it host-side from the test's converter plus GenerateBumpMapSurface and compare against the dS/dT the golden's cell phase implies.

LEAST CERTAIN. That hardware's luminance for a literal component is specifically an unsigned 1.0. What is MEASURED is only that it does not depend on the flag (hardware's four quads agree to its positional floor) and that the unflagged quads of these very captures, which already use 1.0, sit at 310 and 422. Those two together are strong, but they do not exclude a hardware value that happens to round to the same output over this bump texture. The capture that would expose it is one whose luminance range straddles a different output step -- none exists in this corpus -- so the leg is registered as the within-frame identity plus "one-step reaches zero" rather than as a claim about the constant.
